title: Kiosk account binding -- claim and link
description: The wire objects of Section 6, the one-time ceremonies that bind an AI assistant to an existing operator account: claim, an RFC 8628 device grant, and link. Both need the human's approval and a valid possession proof. The two /oauth/* requests are form-encoded and have no schema here; their error answer has one.

deviceAuthorization.description: Section 6.1 step 1: the answer to POST <endpoint>/oauth/device_authorization. All six members are required, also the two that RFC 8628 makes optional.

device_code.description: The opaque code the AI assistant polls with. Never shown to the human.

user_code.description: The short code the human types at the verification page.

verification_uri.description: The operator's session-authenticated approval page (Section 15.8), which names the access the approval hands over.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with the `user_code` already carried, so the human does not have to type it.

interval.description: Seconds the AI assistant waits between polls. A poll that arrives sooner may be answered `slow_down`.

deviceTokenResponse.description: Section 6.1 step 3: the success answer to POST <endpoint>/oauth/token. The bound principal (`user_id`, `agent_id`) is in the access token's claims.

access_token.description: The access token. Its claims are auth.schema.json#/$defs/accessTokenClaims.

token_type.description: Always "DPoP": the token is bound to the key that signed the poll (Section 5.6).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

scope.description: The approving human's role, as the scope that RFC 6749 Section 5.1 grants. It is present only when the binding carries a role, and never null. An AI assistant MUST NOT treat its absence as an error.

oauthError.description: Section 6.1: the error answer of both /oauth/* endpoints, the one error on this wire that is not an RFC 9457 problem document. The status is 400 for every code except `invalid_client`, which is 401.

error.description: The OAuth error code. A closed vocabulary: an operator MUST NOT emit anything outside it, or an AI assistant polling this ceremony has a branch it cannot take.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail. An AI assistant branches on `error` and never on this string.

linkCode.description: Section 6.2 -- the 201 answer to POST <endpoint>/auth/link, called on the operator's own session by the signed-in human. 201 rather than 200 because the call MINTS a redeemable single-use credential.

link_code.description: A long opaque token, paste-grade -- the human hands it to their AI assistant. Stored hashed, single-use, short-TTL and attempt-capped (Section 6.3).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the link code expires.

claimRequest.description: Section 6.2 -- the body of POST <endpoint>/auth/claim, which redeems a link code. The possession proof is REQUIRED, so a leaked code alone can never bind a key its holder does not control.

public_key.description: The AI assistant's public key, PEM-encoded.

signed.description: The possession proof of Section 5.2, as a compact RS256 JWS.

claimResponse.description: Section 6.2: the 201 answer to POST <endpoint>/auth/claim, in the shape of the register answer. A new key, a rebound key and a repeated bind give answers that cannot be told apart (Section 6.3).

unlinkRequest.description: Section 6.3 -- the body of POST <endpoint>/auth/unlink, called on the operator's own session. The response is 204 No Content and carries no body at all, which is why no response object appears here.

agent_id.description: The bound AI assistant to deactivate. Its tokens stop verifying and /auth/login answers 404 (Section 15.4).
